title: UK Heatwave Breaks a Record — And It’s Not Over Yet!
summary:
Have you ever felt so hot you thought you might melt? That’s how a lot of people in England are feeling right now! The country is in its third heatwave of the year, and on Thursday, temperatures soared to 35.1°C (95°F) in Wisley, Surrey. That’s hot enough to fry an egg on the sidewalk — though we don’t recommend trying it!

Here’s the record-breaking part: this year has already had eight days where the temperature reached at least 34°C. That beats the old record from 1976 and 2020. And guess what? Another scorcher is expected on Friday!

Because of the heat, health alerts have been extended to cover almost all of England. These alerts mean the heat could make people sick and put extra pressure on hospitals and ambulance services. The NHS says many ambulance crews are super busy. Trains are also having trouble — some rail companies are telling people to avoid traveling unless it’s really necessary. Why? Because when tracks get too hot, they can bend, which is dangerous. Some trains have been canceled, and others have to go slower.

Even Wimbledon tennis players are feeling it! They’re getting extra water, iced towels, and umbrellas during breaks. The heat is expected to last until Sunday, and maybe even into next week. So if you’re in England, stay cool, drink lots of water, and maybe find a fan!
why_it_matters: Extreme heat can affect your health and daily activities, just like how a very hot day at your school might mean staying indoors, drinking extra water, or even a day off.

background_read: Heatwaves happen when temperatures stay very high for several days. The UK Met Office (the country’s weather service) often issues health alerts to warn people about dangers from extreme heat.
The NHS (National Health Service) is the government-run health system that provides free medical care in the UK.
Wimbledon is the world’s oldest and most famous tennis tournament, held every summer in London, and players sometimes struggle with very hot weather.
Article_Structure: WHO: People in England, the NHS, train companies, and Wimbledon tennis players.
WHAT: A record-breaking heatwave brought temperatures of 35.1°C, causing health alerts and travel problems.
WHERE: England, with the hottest temperature recorded in Wisley, Surrey.
WHY: Extreme heat can make people ill and cause train tracks to bend, leading to cancellations and slower services.

perspectives.description: They are worried because the hot weather can make elderly people and children very sick, putting extra pressure on hospitals and ambulance crews.
They are struggling because the heat can bend metal tracks, making trains unsafe, so they have to cancel or slow down trains to protect passengers.
They are helping tennis players by giving them extra cold water, iced towels, and umbrellas during breaks so they can keep playing safely in the heat.
